events.title: Trump hosts crypto executives at the White House
events.what: President Trump hosted Ripple's Garlinghouse, Coinbase's Armstrong, ICE's Sprecher, Robinhood's Tenev, and Kraken's Sethi — with SEC Chair Atkins in the room — one day after regulators unveiled new crypto rules, and publicly pressed Congress to pass the CLARITY Act.
events.why: Set the political stage for the September 15 cloture vote: the White House put its weight behind the market-structure bill with the industry's CEOs standing next to it.

events.title: Nvidia agrees to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B
events.what: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face — the world's largest open-source AI model hub (13M users, 2.5M models, 950K datasets) — for $12.9 billion, tripling its $4.5B 2023 valuation. The deal puts the dominant AI chipmaker in control of the platform where most AI agents' models are discovered, stored, and deployed.
events.why: The model layer of the machine economy gets a tollbooth operator. Combined with Stripe/OpenRouter ($7B+) and AWS agent payments GA, this is the third major infrastructure consolidation move in twelve weeks — and the clearest signal yet that open, permissionless machine access is being bought and gated by incumbents.

events.title: Congress reconvenes — 14 working days to election recess
events.what: Lawmakers return from August recess with only 14 working days before the October election recess.
events.why: Every pending crypto and agent-payment bill has to move in this window or wait out the election.

events.title: Cloudflare default-blocks mixed-use AI crawlers
events.what: Crawlers that blend search, AI training, and agent use get blocked by default on ad-hosting pages for new customers, new sites, and all free-plan sites. AI companies had until today to separate their crawlers.
events.why: The open web starts gating machine traffic at the edge — and paid, identified access (the thing x402 sells) becomes the sanctioned path in. Cloudflare's pay-per-crawl marketplace is evolving into pay-per-use alongside it.

events.title: CLARITY Act cloture vote in the Senate
events.what: Procedural vote on whether to limit debate and advance the digital-asset market-structure bill to the Senate floor. Needs 60 votes; a failed cloture vote could effectively kill the bill this Congress.
events.why: This is the rulebook for which agency regulates digital-asset markets — including a DeFi trading framework and stablecoin yield rules that shape how agent money is allowed to work.

events.title: Korea Blockchain Week 2026 — Seoul
events.what: Asia's premier Web3 conference at Walkerhill, Seoul: industry leaders, entrepreneurs, and institutional investors on blockchain, AI, and digital-asset regulation.
events.why: The fall conference corridor opens here — announcements seeded at KBW tend to detonate at TOKEN2049 the following week.

events.title: TOKEN2049 Singapore
events.what: The world's largest crypto and Web3 conference — ~25,000 attendees from 160 countries at Marina Bay Sands, with TOKEN2049 Week running October 5–11.
events.why: If there's a major agent-payments or x402 ecosystem announcement brewing, this is the stage it lands on. Ends one day before the Bitcoin cycle pattern's projected turning point.

events.title: Bitcoin 1,064/364-day cycle — projected turning point
events.what: The widely circulated 1,064-day-rise / 364-day-decline pattern (2015→2017→2018→2021→2022→Oct 6 2025 ATH) projects its next turning point around this date — roughly 364 days after the October 6, 2025 all-time high.
events.why: A pattern with n=3 is a rhyme, not a law — but half the market trades like it believes it, which makes the window itself an event. Full date math in our write-up.

events.title: GENIUS Act stablecoin rules — comment period closes
events.what: Treasury's licensing regime for payment-stablecoin issuers closes its Federal Register comment docket.
events.why: The comment docket is the earliest signal of which stablecoin issuers will seek licenses — and whose settlement rail gets complicated. Watch for the issuer behind your rail.

events.title: Tory Burch Fellows 2027 deadline
events.what: Applications close for the 2027 Fellows cohort ($5k + workshop + network, ~120 fellows).
events.why: Revenue gate: requires $75k+ annual revenue from a woman-majority-owned US business. Apply the year the number clears.

events.title: Verizon Digital Ready: last day for the 2 prerequisite courses
events.what: Two courses or events completed by this date unlock the $10k grant application (10 winners a month, June–December).
events.why: Apply once and the application stays in every remaining monthly pool.

events.title: ERCOT data-center audit reports due
events.what: Audit reports on up to 300 proposed Texas data centers are due — disclosures of financing, water, power plans, and ownership. New large-load approvals are paused until the audit completes.
events.why: The first honest census of how much of the 474 GW interconnection queue is real. Whatever survives disclosure is the true footprint of the machine economy in Texas.

events.title: ERCOT presents data-center audit results
events.what: ERCOT presents the audit findings publicly, one week after reports come due.
events.why: Expect the headline number — how many of ~300 proposed sites are credible — and the shape of whatever approval process replaces the pause.

events.title: FedEx Small Business Grant Contest typically opens
events.what: Ten US small businesses get ~$30k plus FedEx Office credit; window usually runs Jan–Mar.
events.why: Needs an active FedEx business shipping account that currently ships. Decide by January whether to open one.

events.title: Cartier Women's Initiative 2028 call opens (approx.)
events.what: Up to $100k plus a year-long fellowship for women-led impact businesses.
events.why: Gates: $50k–$5M revenue last fiscal year and a team of 5–250. Calendar, not a to-do, until then.
